Account summary: LumenKeep (mid-sized enterprise insurance-tech platform) pursuing private VPC deployment for all inference workloads. Strong compliance bar — must satisfy EU data residency for EEA customers and strict audit/log retention. CTO (R. Alvarez) repeated: 'No model tokens or raw customer PII can leave our VPC or be stored in a third-party S3 without encryption and attestable key control.'

Recent timeline and activities:
- 2026-01-15: Intro discovery call (Jordan + Priya). Covered basic latency targets and use cases.
- 2026-01-20: NDA in place. Sent initial Redwood architecture overview.
- 2026-02-02: Security questionnaire (vendor SQA) submitted by LumenKeep. They flagged KMS ownership and audit log retention as critical.
- 2026-02-18: Deep dive (Fireflies ID ff_2026-02-18_0012). Discussed mTLS between customer app and Redwood Private ingress, mutual certs and private CA options.
- 2026-03-05: KMS integration call with security (ff_2026-03-05_0047). Customer prefers customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS KMS & HSM-backed keys for key origin-of-truth.
- 2026-03-10: Demo of Redwood Console audit log export; LumenKeep asked about SIEM integration (Splunk & S3 bucket with restricted access).

Encryption posture details (customer emphasis):
- In-transit: Require mutual TLS (mTLS) for all connections into the Private control plane; TLS1.3 minimum. They also want mTLS for intra-availability-zone traffic and between worker nodes and control-plane endpoints. Discussed private CA vs customer-supplied certs.
- At-rest: Full-disk encryption on nodes plus envelope encryption for model weights and KV cache. They require that token caches and prompt history be encrypted with customer-managed keys.
- KMS & key rotation: Customer demands CMKs in their own AWS account (or HSM in their on-prem HSM). Key rotation cadence: quarterly rotation with automated key rewrap; must provide audit trail for key lifecycle. Need clear rollback story and emergency key-rotation playbook.
- Secrets management: Centralize secrets in HashiCorp Vault (primary) with AWS Secrets Manager as fallback. Redwood to provide Terraform modules and runbooks for Vault integration, short-lived signed certs for mTLS issuance.
- Audit logging & retention: All request/response metadata (no PII) must be logged to a customer-controlled S3 with 7y retention; logs must be tamper-evident and forwarded to Splunk via secure forwarder. Need support for redaction rules and token-masking in logs.
- Data residency: Model artifacts and any persistent storage for EEA customer data must remain in eu-west-1 or customer-controlled on-prem storage.

POC plan and success metrics:
- 2-week private VPC POC in customer AWS account (dedicated subnet and private endpoints).
- Deliverables: architecture diagram, KMS integration proof (CMK usage), audit-log pipeline to S3+Splunk, end-to-end mTLS demo, CIR (compliance & infra readiness) checklist.
- Success metrics: p50 latency <200ms for short-chat (max seq 512), sustained throughput 300 rps per model shard at P95 <350ms, zero unencrypted persistent token storage, audit log completeness >=99%.

Questions / open items for Redwood team:
- Provide detailed key-rotation process for envelope keys and rewrap timeline.
- Confirm support for customer-supplied CA and automatic cert rotation via Vault.
- Provide redaction/tokenization options for request/response logs (config + examples).
- Legal: sample data residency clause and subprocessing flow for EU customers.
